_about: Field terms for F132, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

transfer-entropy.definition: the information, in bits, that the past of one series adds about the next value of a second series beyond what the second series' own past already gives; a larger value one way than the other is commonly read as the direction of influence
transfer-entropy.excludes: plain correlation or mutual information, which are the same in both directions, and any proof of a physical cause

known-answer-test.definition: a test of a method on a case where the true answer is fixed by physics or by construction, so that any wrong reading is a fault of the method
known-answer-test.excludes: agreement with another method, which can share the same fault

ksg-conditional.definition: the k-nearest-neighbour estimate of information from samples given by Kraskov, Stoegbauer and Grassberger and extended to conditional information by Frenzel and Pompe, here with 4 neighbours and the maximum norm
ksg-conditional.excludes: estimates that first bin the data into histograms

iaaft.definition: a copy of a series built by repeated rounds of Fourier phase randomisation and rank reordering, so that it keeps both the original spectrum, and with it the autocorrelation, and the original set of values, while its timing against any other series is lost
iaaft.excludes: a shuffle of single years, which destroys the autocorrelation

high-pass.definition: a filter that keeps fast variation and removes slow trends; here each series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years

detection-rate.definition: the share of sites at which the score in one direction beats its own surrogates at p 0.05 or below
detection-rate.excludes: a rate corrected for testing 135 sites, which is reported separately

direction-accuracy.definition: the share of sites at which the climate-to-ring score is larger than the ring-to-climate score; 0.5 is what a coin would give

block-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by resampling whole 2 degree blocks of sites with replacement, so that neighbouring sites that share climate move together and the interval is not too narrow
block-bootstrap.excludes: a bootstrap over single sites, and a binomial interval that treats sites as independent

site-pairing.definition: a control in which each ring series is paired with the climate of a random site at least 1,000 km away, so that real coupling is removed while both series keep their own form
site-pairing.excludes: pairings with nearby sites, which share regional climate

time-reversal.definition: the same test run on both series read backwards in time; a method that reads direction from lag order should weaken or flip

ccm.field: nonlinear dynamics and ecology (Sugihara and colleagues 2012)
ccm.definition: a test that rebuilds the state of one series from its own lagged values and asks how well that rebuilt state predicts the other series; the driven series is expected to predict the driver
ccm.excludes: regression of one series on the lagged values of the other

granger.definition: a regression test of whether the past values of one series improve the prediction of another beyond that series' own past; for Gaussian data it is equivalent to transfer entropy
granger.excludes: a test of same-year effects, and proof of a physical cause

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate, here 0.05; the adjusted value is called q
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call
